definition: God founds a society immediately when God's own act, not the act of any envoy or creature, constitutes the society, as by a direct divine institution without a human founder. On this sense an envoy's founding, however authorized, is not God's founding.
note: Rival sense recorded so that the envoy-founding premise cannot pass silently between senses. No corpus statement uses it as its reading of FoundedAsTeachingAuthority; a source defending it (for example an ecclesiology for which only an invisible church is God's own work) would make it a sourced rival.
